sections.overview: Nomada kohli is a West Palearctic cuckoo bee whose documented host is the sweat bee Lasioglossum puncticolle.
sections.identification: A published male diagnosis describes a small dark bee with sparse yellow abdominal markings; structural details help separate it from similar Nomada.
sections.habitat: A Luxembourg record came from a landscape dominated by pasture with some nearby woodland; this single observation does not define its full habitat preferences.
sections.diet: Unlike many Nomada associated with Andrena, N. kohli is reported as a cleptoparasite of Lasioglossum; the host brood cell provides food for the larva.
sections.behavior: The host association with L. puncticolle also appears in regional ecological databases; compare N. basalis, for which Andrena hosts are reported.
sections.reproduction: The published host relationship indicates nest parasitism, but detailed observations of egg laying and larval development were not available.
sections.ecology: Because reproduction depends on a particular Lasioglossum host, N. kohli may be overlooked where that small bee is not identified to species.
sections.conservation: A French regional database marks N. kohli as very rare in its territory; this local status should not be generalized to its full range.
